passage.text: Overall the project is moving at an improved pace with most of the roads completed and procurement of consultancies of component B and C (which were pending for a while) have been awarded in the last 6-9 months. The construction of rural roads has been progressing satisfactorily with about 90% of road works substantially completed. A few roads works under this component have been delayed due to unavailability of land and/or pending forest clearances, but it is expected that all road works will be completed well within the project completion date including those road works which are currently experiencing delays due to forest clearances and land unavailability issues. The Road Sector Modernization, has picked up in the past 6 months, after initial delays, with most of the consultancies now awarded and under implementation phase. These activities need to further speed up to be completed within the project implementation period. The Road Safety Management component is progressing satisfactorily with all procurement completed. Implementation of the Road Safety Demonstration Corridor requires close monitoring to be completed within the project completion period.

passage.header: Notice OP00028953, P130164, India, roads, Request for Expression of Interest, (CONSULTING SERVICES FIRMS SELECTION)
passage.text: REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (CONSULTING SERVICES FIRMS SELECTION) THESTATE OF RAJASTHAN - INDIA RAJASTHAN ROAD SECTOR MODERNIZATION PROJECT (RRSMP) Credit No.: 5310-IN Assignment Title: Consultancy Servicesfor "Setting up Sustainable Road Asset Management System" in Public Works Department, Government of Rajasthan, Jaipur Reference No .: CF/RRSMP/05 This request for expressions of interest follows the general procurement notice for this project that appeared in Development Business, December 2012. The Government of Rajasthan has received a Credit from International Development Association (IDA) toward the cost of the Rajasthan Road Sector Modernization Project, and it intends to apply part of the proceeds of this C redit to payments under the contracts for provision of services for "Setting up Sustainable Road Asset Management System" in Public Works Department, Government of Rajasthan, Jaipur. The objective of the Consultancy assignmentis to establish a computerized sustainable Road Asset Management System (RAMS) building on the existing Road Maintenance Management System (RMMS). The RAMS shall be suitable for preparingprioritized investment and maintenance programs for both constructionand maintenance of state roads using rational criteria for investmentdecision. The scope of the consulting services shall also include butnot limited to: Review the functionalities and usefulness of the existing available road management systems ( RMMS) and (ROMAPS) and make recommendations to modify, improve, upgrade so that it could serve the purposes of a well established Road Asset Management System (RAMS). The RAMS should be capable for decision making in the planning, programming, funding, procurement and in the allocation of resources inroad sector in order to make the best use of public funds in preserving the road networks at an acceptable level of serviceability. The RAMS should be able to (i) identify the needs for road widening, pavement strengthening, bridge-improvement and other rehabilitation and upgrading programs; (ii) prioritize these needs based on economic evaluation using HDM-4 and other factors; and(iii) prepare a multiyear rolling program for network improvement andan Annual Maintenance Plan each year. The RAMS should be able to introduce area wide maintenance contract system for different road classification in the State and other forms of maintenance contracting including Long Term Performance Based Maintenance Contracting (LTPBMC) and promoting social aspects including poverty reduction, employment creation, road safety and community involvement. The RAMS should also be able to prepare projectmonitoring reports, carry out an evaluation of pre-agreed performanceindicators and linkage with GIS. The consultancy contract period is expected to be about 30 months.

In addition, there is a need to improve the overall project management mainly data collection, monitoring and reporting, construction quality assurance and contract management is critical for a successful implementation. The following are immediate actions: 1. the recruitment of the Project Management Consultancy firm, 2. the functionality of the sector modernization task force, which are both legal covenant, yet to be complied with, 3. the operationalization and use of the on-line monitoring and management system, and 4. Appointment of dedicated and qualified PMU and PIU staff to ensure monitoring and quality control contract implementation.

passage.text: 51. A recent impact assessment of rural road connectivity in seven states including Rajasthan 2 3 by the Planning Commission Government of India had revealed that the improvement or provision of rural road connectivity had resulted in many fold socio-economic benefits to the villagers. With this background, the entire benefit assessment for Rajasthan State rural roads is centered on the results of the Gol Planning Commission Study findings with the focus in the following domains: (i) Increased household income from agriculture and non- agriculture based activities; (ii) Creation of additional employment opportunities; (iii) Better vehicle ownership and increased travel for work and social trips resulting in reduced travel time and vehicle operating cost; and (iv) promoting the formation of human capital through improved access to education and health facilities. However, for analysis purpose, the education and health 23 Evaluation Study on Rural Roads Component of Bharat Nirman, Programme Evaluation Organization Planning Commission Government of India, New Delhi, May, 2010 benefits were not considered on account of double counting. For the remaining available appropriate quantitative parameters arrived from the evaluation study in the state were used to estimate the project benefits. The total benefits from new road provision are closely correlated with the number of people served by those roads.

passage.header: Notice OP00028956, P130164, India, roads, Request for Expression of Interest, (CONSULTING SERVICES FIRMS SELECTION)
passage.text: REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (CONSULTING SERVICES FIRMS SELECTION) THESTATE OF RAJASTHAN - INDIA RAJASTHAN ROAD SECTOR MODERNIZATION PROJECT (RRSMP) Credit No.: 5310-IN Assignment Title: Consultancy Services for "Modernization of Engineering Practices and Business Procedures" in Public Works Department, Government of Rajasthan, Jaipur Reference No .: CF/RRSMP/03 This request for expressions of interest follows the general procurement notice for this project that appeared in Development Business, December 2012. The Government of Rajasthan has received a Credit from International Development Association (IDA) toward the cost of the Rajasthan Road Sector Modernization Project, and it intends to apply part of the proceeds of this C redit to payments under the contracts for provision of services for "Modernization of Engineering Practices and Business Procedures" in the Public Works Department, Government of Rajasthan, Jaipur. The objective of the Consultancy assignmentis to introduce modern project preparation and management practices, design and construction standards, new technologies specifically to promote cost-effective road construction for low trafficked roads (about 50,000 kilometers) , improved procurement procedures, and PWD-wide procurement and contract management manual. The broad scope of services shall include but not limited to: Review engineering design and construction standards currently being used for different categories of roads, and recommend appropriate design and construction standards which are safe, affordable and more relevant to traffic demands, local site conditions, environmental requirements, social needs, and have adequate design life and high economic rate of return. Recommend new and appropriate technologies specifically for low trafficked roads (about 50,000 km) promoting use of local resources, applying modern engineering practices, and introducing cost effective use of equipment and construction materials. Make recommendations and propose a time based action plan with cost estimate for setting up of a design unit within PWD, which is capable of using modern design software packages aimed at producing safe, reliable and cost-effective structural designs for different types of buildings, roads and bridges. Review the current business procedures being used in PWD for carrying out field surveys, engineering studies, laboratory testing, technical planning, preparation of project design reports, cost estimates, e-procurement, award of contracts, construction management, financial management, environmental and social management, monitoring and impactevaluation and recommend improvements, modifications and changes based on modern engineering practices to ensure that the Client receives the best value of money spent.

passage.header: PAD, P130164, India, roads, Annex 3.B, ¶63, p.59
passage.text: 63. Environmental Issues. The rural road works and road safety interventions on selected road corridors are likely to create some adverse environmental impacts, particularly during the construction stage. While the adverse impacts are likely to be fairly limited in the local context, the exact nature and magnitude of impacts will vary in accordance to the location and type of engineering intervention. Deficiencies in planning and design of sub-projects can lead to insufficient arrangements to conserve natural drainage pattern leading to impairment to or worsening of the local/regional drainage. On the whole, the typical key likely impacts from the operation include: i) felling of some limited number of roadside trees; (ii) adverse impacts on water resources, including from silt flow during execution of works; (iii) soil erosion; (iv) construction phase impacts, including those related to camp site operation, dust generation, and pollution from plants, machinery, and vehicles and disposal of debris/other construction wastes; (v) appropriate management of materials (such as aggregates, sand, water, earth); (vi) safety concerns during construction works and due to increased traffic speeds during operation for both road-users and road-side residents and; (vii) the potential for poorly planned or managed development induced by the improved roads. In view of the project's potential impacts on the environment, the Bank's OP 4.01 on Environmental Assessment and OP 4.11 on Physical Cultural Resources have been triggered, and the project is designated as Category B. 63. Diversion of some forest land may also be required for widening/spot improvement in case of sub-projects involving safety interventions. More so, as part of Component B (Road Sector Modernization and Performance Enhancement), various sector level initiatives would be supported under the project. These include improving policy framework, strengthening of existing road sector policies and strategies, modernization of engineering practices and business procedures and creating asset management system to prepare prioritized plans for both construction and maintenance of state roads. While no civil works will be financed under the project on roads passing through designated protected areas, the larger institutional development plan for the road sector in Rajasthan would need to address the issues of biodiversity management in the interest of road user safety, environmental sustainability and tourism related reasons. Appropriate strategies and mechanisms will have to be built into the institutional systems to ensure that the over-all network planning/development and road selection/construction takes into account such factors.

passage.text: 9. A household is endowed with labour, land and other assets, which it supplies to productive activities, either in the household's own enterprises or those run by others. A new all- weather road will raise export prices and reduce import prices. Hence, income (and welfare) will rise, even if households stick to their old plans. In fact, households will normally respond to these new opportunities in various ways: by changing cropping patterns and farming techniques; by switching into livestock activities; by choosing new marketing channels; and by taking up non- farm business and employment. In Rajasthan, the agricultural productivity had increased by 18.23% due to the road connectivity from INR 16850 per acre to INR 19923 per acre and 24.57% increase in income from non-farm activities (from INR 19050 per household to INR 23730 per household). For the present analysis, the increase in household income from (i) agriculture and (ii) non agriculture (as expressed by the beneficiaries due to the rural road connectivity) was captured by converting in to per capita unit with the help of available data on average increase in agriculture productivity and non-agriculture sources, average landholding, average household size with respect to Rajasthan state, as shown in Table 15 below. Increase in per capita income in terms of weighted average through agriculture and non- agriculture based activities was estimated to INR 1954 at 2013 price levels. Table 15: Details of Estimated Increase in Per capita Annual Income due to Rural Road Connectivity in Rajasthan Average Increase in Agricultural 3073 Income / Acre Rs.

Procurement Setup in the Project Management Unit of CE (PMGSY): All Procurement matters are finalized in accordance with the powers delegated in the Schedule of Power (Annexure XIII) of PWF & AR. The Government of Rajasthan has applied for a Credit from International Development Association (IDA) toward the cost of the Rajasthan Road Sector Modernization Project, and it intends to apply part of the proceeds of this C redit to payments under the contracts for provision of services of Project Management Consultancy to assist the implementation of the project. The consulting services ("the services") include assisting the Public Works Department (PWD) of Rajasthan to efficiently manage the project such that each and every envisaged activity of the project is completed within the planned timeline cost, prescribed standards of quality and in full compliance of the WB guidelines and applicable Employer's acts, rules and regulations. The PMC will be responsible in advising, assisting and acting on behalf of the PWD when so authorized, for the effective management of the Project. passage.text: REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (CONSULTING SERVICES FIRMS SELECTION) THE STATE OF RAJASTHAN - INDIA RAJASTHAN ROAD SECTOR MODERNIZATIONPROJECT (RRSMP) Credit No.: 5310-IN Assignment Title: Consultancy Services for "Engagement of Non- Governmental Organization (NGOs) for Road Safety Education and Awareness Program Covering 33 districts in the state of Rajasthan. Reference No .: CF/RRSMP/08, CF/RRSMP/09, CF/RRSMP/11 to CF/RRSMP/15 This request for expressions of interest follows the general procurement notice for this project that appeared in Development Business, December 2012. The Government of India (GOI) has received a Credit from International Development Association (IDA) toward the cost of the Rajasthan Road Sector Modernization Project (RRSMP), and it intends to apply part of the proceeds for consulting services. The Consulting Services ("the Services") include " Road Safety Education and Awareness Program " in Public Works Department, Government of Rajasthan, Jaipur. The objective of the assignment is to contribute to the reduction of road traffic accidents and fatalities through launching an education and awareness program. This objective will be achieved through addressing the following key areas. Develop and disseminate information on the risks associated to road traffic, good practices in road safety among rural and semi-urban population. Promote safe road user behaviour, improve knowledge and change road safety habits/attitudes of road users. Develop rural representatives as mentors and communicators to spread awarenessabout various aspects of road safety among rural population. Make communities aware that road safety issues are a major community concern Activelyengage community in identifying their road safety problems and solutions Develop capacity and establish linkages with road safety institutions enablingthem to assist the communities to plan, manage and sustain their own road safety initiatives E ducate people about proper use of available road safety engineering facilities Make drivers aware about road safety The scope of the services shall also include but not limited to: 1. The NGO will develop a Model Awareness Program (MAP) for dissemination at the Panchayat/Block level. MAP would inter-alia cover Audio visual presentations, Films in local language, Interactive games, quizzes, Folk songs. Also, NGO would put value addition in the Print materials already available with the department.

passage.text: REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST (CONSULTING SERVICES FIRMS SELECTION) THE STATE OF RAJASTHAN - INDIA RAJASTHAN ROAD SECTOR MODERNIZATION PROJECT (RRSMP) Credit No.: 5310-Ln AssignmentTitle: Consultancy Services for "Independent Technical Audit" (ITA) Reference No .: CF/RRSMP/06 This request for expressions of interest follows the general procurement notice for this project that appeared in Development Business, December 2012. The Government of Rajasthan has applied for a Credit from International Development Association (IDA) toward the cost of the Rajasthan Road Sector Modernization Project, and it intends to apply part of the proceeds of this C redit to payments under the contracts for provision of services of Independent Technical Audit of the project. The services of technical examiners will be required to provide regular technical assistance and monitoring services for quality assurance, and contract administration for about 2500 kms. of rural roads that are to be constructed in the state of Rajasthan under the proposed project, covering the 21 districts of the state. The criteria of selection of the project roads as well as the design and construction standards have been worked-out. However, these are broadly based on IRC publication Rural Road Manual (SP:20) or IRC:SP:72-2007. The overall key objectives of Independent Technical Audit are to: a) shall identify faults, omissions, inconsistencies, ambiguities in the designs and estimates of the rural roads through a 100% review. In particular, the review shall examine the overall cost-effectiveness, adequacy and reliability of field tests, b) shall review on a sample basis the bid documents including the specifications, provisions for quality control, special conditions of the contracts to ensure that the bid documents adequately and reliability reflect the various works required, c) shall visit each work at regularintervals to monitor Field laboratories, technical staff, laboratory equipment, quality control tests being performed, records and reliability of the quality control tests, Setting-out of the works, implementation of the geometric design standards, Quality of supervision and contract administration by the PWD d) shall provide advisory services to the PWD on quality assurance, project supervision, and contract management for the Works. The assignment would last for about 36 months. The Government of Rajasthan through the [contact removed] (PMGSY), PWD now invites eligible consulting firms ("consultants") ") to indicate theirinterest in providing the Services. Interested Consultants should provide information demonstrating that they have the required qualifications and relevant experience to perform the Services. The shortlisting criteria are: a) General experience in Technical Auditof infrastructure projects in last five years

On May 12th, 2011, Rajasthan launched the SUGAM Call Centre in the State Secretariat. The State's Department of Administrative Reforms and Grievances (DARPG) is the nodal department for implementation of this project. The Call Centre accepts complaints through telephone, email and by regular mail. . All twenty-three departments of the state including the PWD are linked on this system, which is also been linked to the Chief Minister's Videoconference based grievance redressal system (e-samadhan) and all the thirty-three District Collectorates. The system has language interfaces both for Hindi and English. . Complaints forwarded by the GOI's Central Public Grievance Redressal and Management System (CPGRAMS - pg.portal.gov.in) to the GOR are also tracked and monitored automatically through this system. . Grievances are scrutinized, registered and instantly transmitted online to the concerned authorities at the Secretariat level, District level and Sub-District level, whereupon the authorities input their replies within 15 days. An important feature of the system is that if a complaint is lodged with any of the departments, it can also be viewed by the District Collector of the concerned district to which the complaint relates. Similarly any complaint lodged at any district can be viewed by the concerned Head of the department. This facilitates effective monitoring of grievances. * SUGAM has been shortlisted for e-India Public Choice Award in the Category of Government to Citizen (G2C) Governance Indicative Costs
